newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Gas oil firmer, jet trades lower.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Gas oil firmer, jet trades lower.

text.p: Singapore gas oil traded slightly higher on Monday as a Singapore trader continued its purchases, while jet fuel was 30 cents lower, traders said.
They said physical gas oil continued to set the tone as swaps players eye the movement of the Singapore player who has bought over 14 million barrels over the past month.
Swaps gas oil for May gained five cents to be last quoted at $25.80-$25.90 per barrel, after a volatile trading day.
The sister company of the Singapore trader bought two 150,000-barrel physical cargoes from a US major--$27.00 a barrel for May 17-21 lifting free-on-board (fob) and $27.40 for May 6-10.

The local trader also continued to buy jet fuel after buying 600,000 barrels last week. On Monday, the trader purchased another 100,000 barrels at $25.00 per barrel for May 17-21 lifting fob from a European major, compared with $25.30 last Thursday. A US trader sold to a Japanese trader at $24.60 for May 6-10 lifting.
Traders said the local traders have so far lifted more than seven million barrels of gas oil and jet fuel without any problems.
India has yet to issue its gas oil and kerosene tenders for June delivery, which traders said was rather late compared with previous tenders.
But India has issued a tender, closing April 24, to buy 25,000 tonnes of aviation turbine fuel for May 11-20 delivery, cost-and-freight Bombay.

Sri Lanka has also issued a tender, closing April 23, to buy 85,000 barrels of gas oil and 60,000 barrels of illuminating kerosene for May 10-12 delivery, c-and-f Trincomalee. Sources in Colombo said state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp would meet again this week to issue another gas oil/jet fuel tender for mid-May delivery.
